genxml.title: SGI HPC1 peripheral controller (Indigo, R3000 and R4000 boards)
genxml.doc: The first-generation peripheral controller of the Indigo: Ethernet, SCSI and parallel-port DMA channels, the DSP audio interface, an endian and revision byte, the auxiliary byte that bit-bangs the serial EEPROM, and the decode of the peripheral windows behind it (Ethernet, SCSI, serial, clock, interrupt controller). Offsets are from the start of one HPC1 window; the primary HPC1 sits at physical 1fb80000. Every register sits in a 32-bit slot and a narrower register uses the byte lane its field bits name. Grades say how each item was derived: established means read in a shipped IRIX driver object, the shipped developer header, a PROM image or a public driver as the source records; inferred means a reasoned reading, with the reasoning in devices/hpc1/README.md. No specification for the HPC1 is held.

struct.name: ENET_PROBE
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: The word at the window base. Software probes it with a guarded read to find out whether a controller is present at the slot; what the word holds is not stated.

struct.name: ENET_XCOUNT
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Transmit count register. The driver's register dump prints it and nothing writes it; its meaning is not settled.

struct.name: ENET_CXBP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Current transmit buffer pointer, by the dump label. Read by the register dump only; no driver writes it.

struct.name: ENET_NXBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Next transmit buffer descriptor pointer: the physical address of the descriptor the transmit channel fetches next. Software writes the head of the queue here, with bits 31:29 clear, before it starts the channel.

struct.name: ENET_XBC
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Transmit byte count of the descriptor in progress. Named by the dump and by the public driver; no driver reads it in a decision.

struct.name: ENET_XPNTR
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Transmit FIFO pointer, by the dump label. Only dumped.

struct.name: ENET_XFIFO
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Transmit FIFO data port, by the dump label. Only dumped.

struct.name: ENET_CXBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Current transmit buffer descriptor pointer. Both drivers load it with the same address they put in the next-descriptor pointer when they start or restart the channel.

struct.name: ENET_CPFXBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Current first transmit buffer descriptor pointer: the first descriptor of the frame being sent. Written with the queue head at a restart.

struct.name: ENET_PPFXBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Previous first transmit buffer descriptor pointer. Named by the dump and the public header; neither driver writes it.

struct.name: ENET_INTDELAY
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Receive interrupt delay count. Bit 24 set (0x01000000) disables the delay; the IRIX driver writes that value at initialisation and writes its tunable delay when it re-enables the delay after a received frame.

struct.name: ENET_TRSTAT
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Transmit status and channel start. Bit 22 starts the transmit channel when written one and reads one while the channel is running. The bits above it carry the SEEQ transmit status byte; the drivers only test bit 22.

struct.name: ENET_RCVSTAT
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Receive status and channel start. Bit 14 starts the receive channel when written one and reads one while it runs; the other bits of the upper byte carry the Ethernet chip's receive status.

struct.name: ENET_CTL
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: Ethernet channel control: reset, interrupt clear and loopback. Reading bit 1 reports a pending interrupt.

struct.name: ENET_RCOUNT
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Receive count register, by the dump label. Only dumped.

struct.name: ENET_RBC
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Receive byte count of the descriptor in progress.

struct.name: ENET_CRBP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver
struct.doc: Current receive buffer pointer, by the dump label.

struct.name: ENET_NRBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Next receive buffer descriptor pointer: physical address of the first descriptor the receive channel fetches. Software writes the head of the ring here, with bits 31:29 clear, before it sets the receive start bit.

struct.name: ENET_CRBDP
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Current receive buffer descriptor pointer. The IRIX driver loads it with the ring head at start and its watchdog reads it to see whether the channel has moved.

struct.name: ENET_RPNTR
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: Receive FIFO pointer, by the dump label. The PROM's early test stores the byte 0x5a to its low byte lane and reads the register after it, without a recorded check.

struct.name: ENET_RFIFO
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: Receive FIFO data port, by the dump label.

struct.name: SCSI_BC
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: SCSI channel byte count of the descriptor being moved. The channel loads it from the descriptor; software does not write it in normal operation.

struct.name: SCSI_CBP
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: SCSI channel current buffer pointer: the physical address of the data being moved, loaded from a descriptor.

struct.name: SCSI_NBDP
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: SCSI next descriptor pointer. Software writes the physical address of the first descriptor, then the control register with the start bit; the channel then walks the chain by itself.

struct.name: SCSI_CTRL
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: SCSI channel control. The reset bit holds the WD33C93 chip in reset while set. The flush bit drains the channel FIFO and the start bit reads one while the channel is active, so software sets flush and waits for the start bit to read zero.

struct.name: SCSI_PNTR
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: SCSI FIFO pointer register. Present in both headers and in the chip interface table; no driver read or write of it was found.

struct.name: SCSI_FIFO
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: SCSI FIFO data port. No driver access was found.

struct.name: PAR_BC
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX parallel driver
struct.doc: Parallel port byte count with the strobe timing fields. The header gives three seven-bit timing fields at bits 30:24, 22:16 and 14:8; the driver stores a placeholder here before it loads a descriptor.

struct.name: PAR_CBP
struct.from: IRIX developer header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: Parallel current buffer pointer. The PROM's power-on test writes a walking one from bit 27 down to bit 0 and reads each value back, so the low 28 bits are plain storage.

struct.name: PAR_NBDP
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX parallel driver
struct.doc: Parallel next descriptor pointer: the physical address of the first descriptor, written before the control register.

struct.name: PAR_CTRL
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX parallel driver
struct.doc: Parallel port control.

struct.name: PAR_FIFO
struct.from: IRIX parallel driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Parallel FIFO status. Bits 22:16 hold the number of bytes still in the port FIFO; the stop routine drains that many bytes by hand when the count is under four.

struct.name: PAR_DMACFG
struct.from: NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Parallel DMA configuration, named by the public header only. No IRIX object touches it.

struct.name: ENDIAN
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; NetBSD register header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: DMA byte order of each channel and the controller revision. A set bit makes that channel's DMA words and descriptors little-endian; clear leaves them big-endian. Only the low byte is used.

struct.name: SEEQ
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: The Ethernet chip's eight registers, one per 32-bit slot with the byte in bits 7:0; register n is at 0x100 plus 4n. Registers 0 to 5 hold the station address, register 6 is the receive command and status and register 7 the transmit command and status. The registers themselves are in devices/seeq_8003.

struct.name: WD33C93_ADDRESS
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: The WD33C93's address/auxiliary-status port. The chip sits on the 15:8 byte lane of the word: a big-endian byte access is at +2 and a little-endian one at +1.

struct.name: WD33C93_DATA
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: The WD33C93's data port, on the same byte lane.

struct.name: PAR_STATUS
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX parallel driver
struct.doc: Parallel port external status and remote register, one byte in bits 23:16 of the word. A DMA read start stores 1 and a write start stores 3; the reset routine clears it then stores 3.

struct.name: DSP_DMA_COUNT
struct.from: IRIX developer header; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: DSP DMA transfer length in SRAM words. See devices/hollywood-dsp.

struct.name: DSP_GIO_LOW
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: Low 16 bits of the memory-side DMA address.

struct.name: DSP_GIO_HIGH
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: High 16 bits of the memory-side DMA address.

struct.name: DSP_PBUS_ADDR
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: 16-bit peripheral-bus (DSP SRAM) address of the DMA.

struct.name: DSP_DMA_CTRL
struct.from: IRIX developer header; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: DSP DMA control.

struct.name: DSP_COUNTER
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: A free-running 24-bit counter; what it counts is not stated.

struct.name: DSP_HAND_TX
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: Handshake transmit word, written by the DSP for the host.

struct.name: DSP_HAND_RX
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: Handshake receive word, written by the host for the DSP.

struct.name: DSP_INT_STATUS
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: DSP-to-CPU interrupt status: bit 0 end of DMA, bit 1 the DSP wrote the transmit word, bit 2 the DSP read the receive word.

struct.name: DSP_INT_MASK
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: Enable bits for the three DSP interrupt sources.

struct.name: DSP_MISC
struct.from: IRIX developer header; NetBSD register header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: DSP miscellaneous control. The PROM stores 9 (reset with 32K SRAM) at start-up, 1 (reset) while it loads the DSP and 8 (run, 32K SRAM) afterwards.

struct.name: DSP_BURST
struct.from: IRIX developer header; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: DMA burst length and spacing; the fields are not stated.

struct.name: AUX
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; NetBSD register header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: The auxiliary byte: the console LED and the four wires of the serial EEPROM. Bit 0 is shared by the LED and the EEPROM protect-register enable.

struct.name: INT2_WINDOW
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: The interrupt controller window, 64 bytes at 0x1c0. The registers are in the interrupt controller's own unit; the controller is not part of the HPC1.

struct.name: SERIAL_WINDOW
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX serial driver
struct.doc: Four 16-byte blocks of 8-bit registers at 0xd00, 0xd10, 0xd20, 0xd30, each register in its own slot with the byte in bits 7:0 (offset +3 big-endian). Blocks 0 to 2 are Z85C30 serial controllers; block 3 holds the two headphone gain converters. The chip's registers are in its own unit.

struct.name: CLOCK_WINDOW
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: The battery-backed real-time clock window, one 8-bit register per 32-bit slot, accessed by word at the slot. The chip's registers are in its own unit.

struct.name: BOARD_REV
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: Board revision word, in the modem SRAM space. The kernel inverts the word and takes bits 14:12; bit 15 is the header's marker for the HP1 base board.

struct.name: DSP_SRAM
struct.from: IRIX developer header; NetBSD register header; Indigo PROM
struct.doc: The DSP SRAM, one 24-bit word per 32-bit slot, 128 KB.

struct.name: ENET_DESC_W0
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Word 0 of the Ethernet DMA descriptor: flags and byte count. The HPC3 puts the buffer address first and the flags second; the HPC1 order is the reverse.

struct.name: ENET_DESC_W1
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Word 1 of the Ethernet DMA descriptor: the buffer address with the end-of-chain flag.

struct.name: ENET_DESC_W2
struct.from: IRIX Ethernet driver; NetBSD register header
struct.doc: Word 2 of the Ethernet DMA descriptor.

struct.name: SCSI_DESC_W0
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: Word 0 of the SCSI and parallel DMA descriptor. A descriptor is three hardware words in a 16-byte slot; the fourth word is software-only. The words are in the byte order that the endian register selects for the channel.

struct.name: SCSI_DESC_W1
struct.from: IRIX developer header; IRIX kernel
struct.doc: Word 1 of the SCSI and parallel DMA descriptor.

struct.name: SCSI_DESC_W2
struct.from: IRIX developer header
struct.doc: Word 2 of the SCSI and parallel DMA descriptor.
